title: Session Export
description: A completed training session exported by AccelerometerLifting for LLM analysis.

schemaVersion.description: 1.1: velocityLoss_pct is best-to-LAST rep; unmeasured phases are null rather than 0; tempo compliance scores movement digits only; repMetricsComplete reports per-rep coverage. 1.2: a set may carry `geometry`, the resolved direction and sensor mounting its numbers were measured with, plus the provenance of each value. Purely additive — no key from 1.1 changed type or stopped being written, so a 1.1 reader works unchanged against a 1.2 export. 1.3: a session may carry `timeZone`, the device's zone and UTC offset when it was recorded. Also purely additive — `startedAt` and `endedAt` are unchanged and still UTC with a `Z` — so a 1.2 reader works unchanged against a 1.3 export. 1.4: a set's `hr` block is published only from the samples the strap's own report supports. `avgBpm` and `maxBpm` are taken over those samples rather than over every sample; `endOfSetBpm` is present only when the set's FINAL sample is one of them, and is never backfilled from an earlier one; and the whole block is absent when the strap reported nothing usable. NOT purely additive: no key changed type or stopped being written, but `avgBpm` and `maxBpm` are computed over a different population and `endOfSetBpm` names a different sample, so a 1.3 reader comparing these figures across versions is comparing different quantities. 1.5: on a body-weight set, `plannedLoad_kg` is paired on the same scale as `load_kg` — the plan's declared added load plus the same body weight, rather than the added load alone. NOT purely additive for the same reason 1.4 was not: no key changes type or stops being written, but the VALUE `plannedLoad_kg` carries for a body-weight set changes meaning, so a 1.4 reader comparing it against `load_kg` on such a set is comparing quantities that used to disagree on purpose and now do not. 1.6: a set summary may carry `romSpread_pct`, how far the reps of the set disagree with each other about `rom_m`, as a percentage of `meanRom_m`. Purely additive - no key from 1.5 changed type or stopped being written, so a 1.5 reader works unchanged against a 1.6 export. 1.7: a set's `hr` block may carry `minBpm`, the lowest bpm its trusted samples support — the same population `avgBpm` and `maxBpm` already draw from. Purely additive — no existing key changes type or stops being written, so a 1.6 reader works unchanged against a 1.7 export. Computed at export time from the set's own raw HRM stream rather than a stored column, so it is available on every session already recorded, not only ones captured after this version shipped. 1.8: `hrvRmssd_ms` is computed from a de-duplicated R-R series. This strap re-sends its last completed interval at a fixed ~500 ms cadence whenever no new beat has arrived, and every repeat contributed a successive difference of exactly zero; a notification identical to its predecessor is now counted once. NOT purely additive: no key changes type or stops being written, but the VALUE is computed over a different population, so a 1.7 reader comparing this figure across versions is comparing different quantities. On the one worn capture held here the value rises from 11.12 to 12.20 -- +9.7% measured against the OLD value, equivalently 8.8% of the new one -- where those figures are Hrv.rmssdMs over that session's seventeen persisted set streams concatenated into one series. The effect is larger the lower the heart rate, because the re-sent fraction rises as the beat interval lengthens against a fixed cadence. Recorded here because it is not the first such change: #27 altered the same field by about -11% on the same corpus WITHOUT a version bump, which was an error this entry corrects forward rather than repeats. 1.9: a set's `hr` block is published only when the set's own R-R intervals account for at least a third of the time the set covers. A strap that has lost contact holds its last interval and re-sends it, so its intervals cover a fraction of the elapsed time while a worn strap's tile it; a stream that cannot show it was tracking a heart now publishes no `avgBpm`, `maxBpm`, `minBpm` or `endOfSetBpm` rather than a believable resting figure. A stream carrying no R-R intervals at all is NOT affected: it cannot produce this measure, and absence of evidence is not silenced here. This applies RETROACTIVELY to sessions already recorded, which is most of its effect: `avgBpm`, `maxBpm` and `endOfSetBpm` are stored when a set is recorded, so the export re-asks the question of the set's stored raw stream and withholds the whole `hr` block or none of it. A set whose raw stream is no longer stored cannot be re-judged and is published exactly as before. Note for readers comparing sets: an `hr` block carrying `avgBpm` and `maxBpm` but no `minBpm` means the raw stream was unavailable to compute a minimum from -- it is a statement about the archive, NOT a statement that the heart rate never went low. The session-level `heartRate` block is withheld when a session has sets and none of them publishes an `hr` block, because that block is aggregated from the set rows and must not outlive them. NOT purely additive, for the reason 1.4 was not: no key changes type or stops being written, but the population these figures are computed over changes, so a 1.8 reader comparing them across versions is comparing different quantities. 1.10: `velocityLoss_pct` is withheld, rather than published as 0.0, when the last rep the sensor resolved is also the fastest of the set. The figure is best rep to LAST rep, so its reference is a maximum taken over a list that contains its own last element: `best - last` can never be negative, and the quotient reaches exactly 0.0 only when the last rep ties the maximum. A last rep that ties the maximum is also the signature of a spurious final detection -- the sensor being set down, or the lifter getting off the machine, moving faster than any rep -- so the reassuring reading and the artefact could not be told apart. A new key `velocityLossBasis` names which case a set is in, and is present whenever the set resolved any reps at all -- including, and especially, when the figure itself is absent, so that a WITHHELD figure is distinguishable from one an older app version never wrote. NOT purely additive: `velocityLoss_pct` STOPS BEING WRITTEN on sets where 1.9 wrote it, so a 1.9 reader treating a present number as authoritative now finds an absent key rather than a changed value. Applies RETROACTIVELY to sessions already recorded, which is most of its effect: the judgement is re-derived at export time from the set's stored reps rather than read from the stored scalar, the same way 1.9 re-asks its question of the stored raw stream. A genuinely flat set -- one where the lifter really did hold velocity to the last rep -- is withheld too. That is a decision, not an oversight: best-to-last with last equal to best is the degenerate case of the definition and carries no information about fatigue in either direction, and `velocityLossBasis` still reports that the last rep was the fastest. Note for readers parsing this field numerically: the string "1.10" is not the number 1.1 -- float("1.10") collides with schema version 1.1, which is a different contract. Compare it as a string. 1.11: a set may carry `plannedPrep_s` and `prep_s`. Purely additive: no key from 1.10 changed type or stopped being written, so a 1.10 reader works unchanged against a 1.11 export. Both keys are absent on a set that played no prep and on every set recorded before this version. 1.12: a set's per-rep figures cover only the detections whose drive began at or before the set's own `Done` cue. A guided set goes on recording after the metronome stops prescribing: the eleven sets of session 32 that carry both a `Done` cue and an IMU stream keep recording for 4.3 to 13.7 s past it, measured as last sample minus cue. The sensor being put down, unclipped or carried in that window segments as a rep like any other. Those detections are excluded before anything is derived from the rep list, so `repMetrics`, `velocityLoss_pct`, `velocityLossBasis`, `repMetricsComplete`, `reps` on a sensor-counted set and every field of `summary` are computed over a different population of reps. NOT purely additive, for the reason 1.4, 1.8 and 1.9 were not: no key changes type or stops being written, but a 1.11 reader comparing these figures across versions is comparing different quantities. Measured sizes: on the session that found it, set 6's `velocityLoss_pct` moves from 82.6 to 52.1; on three captures of an earlier session, `summary.peakConVel_mps` falls from 1.673 to 0.737, from 1.707 to 0.768 and from 1.261 to 0.910 m/s, and those same three move from `velocityLossBasis` "terminalRepIsFastest" to "measured" -- they were withheld because nothing in the rep list could separate a spurious final detection from a set held flat to the end, and the cue track answers that from outside the rep list. The basis vocabulary itself is unchanged. A set all of whose detections began after the cue publishes no `velocityLossBasis`, which qualifies 1.10's promise that the key is present whenever the set resolved any reps. The boundary is the cue's own timestamp rather than the end of its utterance, which is recorded nowhere, and a detection that straddles the boundary is kept: what makes a movement a rep of the set is that the lifter began it while the set was running. A set whose cue track never says `Done` is not bounded at all and no boundary is invented for it -- an ad-hoc set recorded with the voice guide off, every set recorded before the app wrote cue tracks, and any guided set the lifter ended before the prescription was called through, which is five of the seventeen sets of the session this was measured on. This does not apply retroactively: the exporter re-derives these figures from the STORED rep list, and a stored rep carries durations, velocities, a range and an ordinal index -- an index into the rep list, not into the samples -- but no instant, so an already-recorded row cannot be placed against its own cue track without re-running segmentation over its stored raw IMU stream, which the exporter does not do. Sets recorded before this version publish exactly what they published before. 1.13: `duration_s` on a timed set is the figure the set was RECORDED with, not the seconds its clock measured. A hold or carry now ends when its clock reaches the seconds the set was WORKING TO -- `plannedDuration_s` unless the lifter changed the hold in the change-set dialog, in which case theirs -- so a set that ran to its target publishes `plannedDuration_s` only when the lifter did not change it; a set the lifter ended by hand publishes what it lasted; a set corrected afterwards on the rest screen publishes the corrected figure. NOT purely additive, for the reason 1.4, 1.5, 1.8, 1.9 and 1.12 were not: no key changes type or stops being written, but the VALUE `duration_s` carries changes for the majority case -- under auto-end that is every timed set the lifter does not cut short -- so a 1.12 reader comparing hold seconds across versions is comparing different quantities. What a 1.12 reader may assume and a 1.13 reader may not: that `duration_s` is a measurement of elapsed time, and that `duration_s == plannedDuration_s` is evidence the lifter stopped on the word. What changes in the other direction: under 1.12 a timed set ran until the lifter ended it by hand, so a recorded figure above `plannedDuration_s` was the ordinary case and carried the walk back to the phone inside it. Under 1.13 it is no longer the ordinary case, but it is NOT excluded. A set the lifter ends by hand still publishes what its clock measured, and the tick loop counts one-second delays rather than wall-clock seconds, so a hand-ended set can publish more seconds than were prescribed with no rest-screen correction applied. A `duration_s` above `plannedDuration_s` is therefore not evidence of a stated overage. Corrected and measured seconds are NOT distinguishable in either version: reps publish `repsManual` and there is no counterpart for duration, so a stated figure and a measured one are the same key. This does NOT apply retroactively: `duration_s` is read from the stored `actualDurationS` column rather than re-derived at export time, so a set recorded before this version publishes exactly what it published before, and what changes is which quantity a newly recorded set stores there. No size is stated for the shift: how much of a pre-1.13 hold was phone-retrieval time is a question only a real session answers, and this repository holds no capture of a timed set to measure it from. 1.13 carries a SECOND change, and it is additive where the first is not: a set may carry `repMarks`, the epoch-ms instants at which a rep was counted -- the lifter's taps on a manually counted set, the voice guide's calls on a guided one. No key from 1.12 changes type or stops being written for it, so a reader that ignores `repMarks` reads a 1.13 export exactly as it read a 1.12 one; the `duration_s` warning above is the half of this version that a 1.12 reader must be re-checked against, and this half is not. Two changes share one version because 1.13 was unreleased when the second landed, and minting 1.14 for a key no reader had shipped against would publish a boundary that never existed. `repMarks` is absent, never an empty array, on every set that counted nothing out loud -- which includes every ordinary sensor-counted set and every set recorded before the app stored marks, and those two are not distinguishable from each other. Its length may disagree with `reps`: a rest-screen correction rewrites the count and cannot reach a mark already written, and the guide calls a rep on its own schedule whether or not the lifter followed it. 1.13 carries a THIRD change, additive on the same terms and under the same version for the same reason (#156): a set may carry `sensors`, saying how many accelerometers it was armed with, which roles they carried, which of those reached the raw archive and which one the set's figures came from. What each field means is stated once, at $defs.setSensors. No key from 1.12 changes type or stops being written for it, and it is ABSENT on every ordinary one-sensor set -- so a single-sensor export is byte-for-byte what 1.12 wrote apart from the version string itself, which is written unconditionally and therefore cannot be held identical under any bump at all. In the raw archive the same set gains one CSV per role, named with the role appended to the kind (set01_bench_press_imu-a.csv), and meta.json carries the role-to-file mapping with a per-stream sample count and a rate measured from that stream; a one-sensor set's CSV keeps the name it has always had. 1.13 carries a FOURTH change, additive on the same terms and under the same version for the same reason (#159): a session may carry `sessionRpe`, the lifter's own 1-10 answer to how the whole workout felt, stated once when they finished it. No key from 1.12 changes type or stops being written for it, and it is ABSENT on every session the lifter did not rate as well as on every session recorded before this version -- absence means unrated and must not be read as a low rating. What each field means is stated once, at the property itself, including the warning that matters most for this one: `sessionRpe` and a set's `rpe` are two different instruments whose published ranges overlap, and nothing but their descriptions tells them apart. 1.13 carries a FIFTH change, under the same number because 1.13 was unreleased when that change landed, and this one is NOT additive (#176): `voiceCues` records the rep call the guide MERGES into a stroke's own word, which until now was spoken and written nowhere. Where a rep call has no pause to sit in, the guide says the stroke word and the call as a single utterance -- `Down, Rep 3` -- because the speech engine cancels whatever it was saying when a new utterance arrives; only the stroke word reached the cue track, so on those plans the array named no rep at all. Measured on the session that found it, 16 sets on app 0.1.43: `Rep N` and `Last rep` appear ZERO times in 539 cue rows, on a session where the lifter heard a rep call on every rep after each set's first -- 157 calls spoken and unwritten. They were datable at all only because a carrying stroke gives up its first tempo count to make room for the call, leaving a hole where a `1` should have been: exactly one `1` per set, on all sixteen. What changes for a reader: a newly recorded set's `voiceCues` carries `Rep N` and `Last rep` rows it did not carry before, and the stroke row keeps its own value and gains a SECOND row at the SAME `t_ms` rather than being renamed. A consumer counting or matching stroke rows is unaffected; a consumer counting ALL rows, or assuming one instant is one row, sees a different population. That is the reason this is filed as non-additive and not additive -- no key changes type or stops being written, and the contents of an existing array change, which is the shape 1.4, 1.8, 1.9 and 1.12 each carry. This does NOT apply retroactively: cue rows are stored as they are spoken, so a set recorded before this version publishes exactly the rows it published before, and nothing in a row distinguishes a set that never spoke a call from one that spoke it and did not write it down. The same change decides where `Last rep` is not spoken at all (#173), and a reader needs both halves or the absence is unreadable: on a schedule whose only slot for the warning is the beat the rep ends on, the guide would be warning about a rep with only one stroke of it left, so it says nothing and the terminal `Done` carries the ending alone. The absence of a Last rep row on such a set is therefore a DECISION and not a gap -- which matters because before this version the same absence meant the opposite, a warning spoken and written nowhere, and the two leave identical evidence. Which schedules those are is not readable from the tempo string: the same four digits put the call at the start of the rep on one lift and at its end on another, and a session recorded both. The finished-rep `Rep N` calls are unaffected and still appear on every such set; what a suppressed warning gives back is the tempo count the carrying stroke had given up for it, so the second that used to be silent carries a digit. 1.13 carries a SIXTH change, under the same number because 1.13 was unreleased when that change landed, and it is NOT additive (#157, #174): `plannedReps` and `plannedDuration_s` publish what the PLAN declared, frozen at import, rather than what the lifter left in the change-set dialog's box. Until this version a lifter who dropped a set from 8 to 6 exported plannedReps 6, so no deviation was visible at all; the same set now exports plannedReps 8 beside reps 6. No key changes type or stops being written, but the VALUE both keys carry changes on every set the lifter edited, so a reader comparing a planned figure against a performed one across versions is comparing different quantities. This does NOT apply retroactively: both are read from stored columns, so a set recorded before this version publishes exactly what it published before. What the lifter STATED -- which after #174 may be a count carried from an earlier set of the block -- is still not exported: a reader sees what was prescribed and what was performed, not what was declared in between, which is #157's remaining half. 1.13 carries a SEVENTH change, additive on the same terms and under the same version for the same reason (#177): a set may carry `added`, saying the LIFTER appended it to the exercise mid-session rather than the plan prescribing it. The control sits with the other between-sets decisions, on the rest screen and on READY, and it is repeatable -- adding two sets is adding one twice. No key from 1.12 changes type or stops being written for it, and it is ABSENT on every prescribed set and on every set recorded before database v12, so a reader that ignores `added` reads a 1.13 export exactly as it read a 1.12 one. What each field means is stated once, at the property itself, including the two warnings that matter most: an appended set publishes no `plannedLoad_kg`, `plannedReps` or `plannedDuration_s` because nothing prescribed it, but DOES publish `tempoPrescribed`, `rest_s` and `plannedPrep_s` carried unchanged from the rest of the block, and an absent flag on a session recorded before v12 means "prescribed, or recorded before the app could tell" rather than "prescribed". REMOVING a set is not part of this change and no key says a prescribed set was dropped; a plan's remaining sets going unrecorded is what it always was, an absence. SEVEN CHANGES UNDER ONE VERSION is what an unreleased version number is for, and the count is not itself the warning: exactly three of the seven -- `duration_s`, `voiceCues` and the `plannedReps` / `plannedDuration_s` pair -- are not additive, and a 1.12 reader must be re-checked against those three and need not be re-checked against `repMarks`, `sensors`, `sessionRpe` or `added`. 1.14: a RELEASED boundary, not another change under an open number -- 1.13 shipped in v0.1.44, read at the tag. `warmup` is now a PLAN DECLARATION and no longer a rating. Until this version the only thing that could set it was an effort tile the lifter tapped, and that tile stored `warmup: true` together with `rpe: null`, so the effort of every warm-up set was discarded by construction. From 1.14 the plan declares it, through the plan-schema 1.9 key of the same name, and a warm-up set carries a real `rpe` like any other set -- the empty-bar ramp set of a 500 lb squatter is a warm-up by PURPOSE, and what it felt like is a separate fact worth keeping. NOT purely additive: no key changes type or stops being written, but the published description of `warmup` stops telling a reader to exclude these sets from effort analysis, because after this version that instruction is false. A reader that excludes them from VOLUME or progression is unaffected and the field still supports that. This does NOT apply retroactively: `warmup` is read from a stored column, so a set recorded before this version publishes exactly what it published before -- and on those sessions `warmup: true` with no `rpe` means the app could not record both, NOT that the lifter declined to rate the set. One consequence to read carefully: a set the lifter added mid-session, and any ad-hoc set, publishes no `warmup` at all even when it was a ramp, because nothing declared it and the app offers no control that says so. 1.14 carries a SECOND change, under the same number because 1.14 was unreleased when that change landed and the two are one design (#187), and it is NOT additive either: `rpe` is a 1-to-10 scale whose rungs are ANCHORED DIFFERENTLY ALONG ITS LENGTH. 7 to 10 stay reps in reserve -- 3, 2, 1, none left -- and below them the anchors are load headroom: 6 is 'could have added one equipment increment', 4 is two increments, 1 is much more. On a hold or a carry the same three rungs ask in SECONDS instead, because load headroom is meaningless on a plank. The reason the low end stopped being a rep count is measured rather than stylistic: mean error in calling one's own reps in reserve is 2.05 reps at 1 RIR and 5.15 reps at 5 RIR (Zourdos et al., 2019), so at that distance the error is larger than the claim, while a load figure there is answerable and checkable next session. 2, 3 and 5 are valid values that carry NO tile: the gaps exist so the anchors sort, and a reader meeting one is looking at a real value on the same ruler rather than corrupt data. NOT additive and NOT retroactive: no key changes type or stops being written and no stored value is rewritten, but a newly written low value means something the old scale could not say. THE VALUE TO READ CAREFULLY IS 6. Under 1.13 and earlier the grid offered 6 to 10 only, and 6 was its FLOOR, 'easy, 4+ reps left' -- so it absorbed everything the new 1 and 4 now take, and 46% of this lifter's historical ratings sit on it. It is reused rather than retired to 5 because the standard RPE-to-RIR chart puts 6 at 4 RIR, roughly the state 'could have added one increment' describes, so old values stay interpretable on the same ruler; do not read a pre-1.14 6 as specifically meaning one increment. 7 through 10 are unchanged in meaning across this boundary. The warm-up tile is also gone from that grid, which is the first change above. 1.14 carries a THIRD change, additive, under the same number and for the reason the first two share -- worth restating because it was asked for as 1.15: 1.14 was UNRELEASED WHEN THAT WAS WRITTEN and is not now: v0.1.45 shipped it, read at tag c44f1c531d6343d0071f82c062344e7f4eff950f. The sentence was true of v0.1.44, which shipped 1.13 at tag 7cf6e8c3cc546ab8d64c9fb2be86de2129250b43, and it stopped being true when the next tag was cut. The changes below rode under one number on the strength of it, correctly at the time; that window is closed -- the same rule seven changes rode under 1.13 for. The change (#189): a set may carry `limiter`, why it ended, from a closed vocabulary; and `limiterNote`, the lifter's own words where that answer is `other`. No key from 1.13 changes type or stops being written, and both are absent on every set nobody was asked about and on every set recorded before database v13. A 1.13 reader works unchanged against a 1.14 export for this change. 1.14 carries a FOURTH change (#194), under the same number because 1.14 was unreleased when that change landed, and NOT additive: `warmup` gains a SECOND PRODUCER. Until now the plan declared it and nothing else could; the lifter may now mark or unmark a set on the rest screen, and where the two disagree the lifter's mark wins. No key changes type and no stored value is rewritten, but a 1.13 reader that treats `warmup: true` as 'the plan said so' must be re-checked, which is why this is flagged rather than filed beside the additive changes. The new key `warmupByLifter` says which of the two a given set carries and is absent on every set the lifter never marked, which is every set recorded before database v13. It does NOT publish the plan's overridden declaration: where the mark disagrees, this document carries the answer and its author, and the app's row keeps both. 1.15: `plannedCount` is REMOVED from a set's `sensors` block and `shortfall` is added to it. NOT additive: a reader that requires plannedCount must be changed. The key said how many accelerometers the PLAN prescribed, and no plan prescribes any -- the app records from whatever is connected, one bar sensor writing one stream and two connected units labelled A and B writing two, on every set of every exercise. A key that kept emitting the old default of 1 would tell a reader a coach intended something. `shortfall` carries what the pair used to carry between plannedCount and `count`: "rolesUnassigned" or "rolesCollide", present only when two units were PAIRED and the app could not tell them apart and therefore recorded one stream. The app never opened a link to the second unit in this state, so this says two units are paired and cannot be told apart -- not that both were powered on or in range. That is the distinction this document must keep making, because "there was one sensor" and "there were two and one was unusable" are different facts about a session. The raw archive's meta.json moves with it: `sensorsPlanned` is gone and `sensorsShortfall` is added, carrying the same two words. Exports declaring 1.13 or 1.14 carry plannedCount inside this block; 1.12 and earlier have no sensors block at all, and even at 1.13 and 1.14 only sets that carried a declaration have one. A reader meeting the key should read it as what a plan asked for under a rule that no longer applies. A NOTE ON THIS DOCUMENT ITSELF, true from 1.15 and not before: this schema describes the CURRENT shape only, and 1.15 is the first version to REMOVE a key rather than add one, so a document declaring an earlier version from the enum above is not thereby valid against this file -- a genuine 1.14 export carrying a set's `sensors` block fails here on `plannedCount`, because `setSensors` sets `additionalProperties` false and no longer declares that key. Validate a pre-1.15 export against the copy of this schema published at its own release tag. The enum lists which versions the APP accepts, not which documents this file validates. 1.16: `bottomPause_s` and `topPause_s` measure the turnaround INSIDE a rep, and exactly one of them is published per rep instead of both. NOT additive and this is the version to re-check a reader against: both keys were REQUIRED under 1.15 and neither is now, and the one that is still written carries a different quantity on some lifts than it did. The key that stops being written is whichever end the rep's own BOUNDARY falls on -- `topPause_s` on a lift whose reps start at the top, `bottomPause_s` on a lift whose reps start at the bottom -- because the stillness at that end is not inside the rep at all: it runs from the end of the rep's last detected phase until the next drive begins, so it holds the lifter's rest and nothing in the segmentation separates a hold from a rest. That is what it was publishing. Measured on the capture this was found on, a single-leg press prescribing NO bottom pause published bottomPause_s of 0.02 / 0.10 / 1.57 / 0.33 / 1.29 / 0.06 / 0.08 / 0.01 s, and issue #93 reports the same field reaching 22.73 s on a leg press with a mean of 1.34 s against a median of 0.16 s. The key that IS still written is unchanged in value on every rep that resolved both its phases; it changes only in that it is absent, rather than 0.0, on a rep the segmenter counted from the drive alone, which has one phase and therefore no turnaround. WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, stated because the headline figure in #93 survives it: the published pause is bounded by the two phases THIS REP resolved, so where segmentation merged reps it spans everything between them. One committed leg-press capture resolves 2 detections for 8 performed reps and its second detection carries a 14.27 s turnaround, which is a true statement about that detection and a useless one about the lifter. Read a pause beside the length of `repMetrics` against `reps`; a set whose detections are far under its rep count has pauses that cover the reps it missed. DOES NOT APPLY RETROACTIVELY, and the boundary is when a set was RECORDED rather than when it was exported. `repMetrics` is built at export time, but from the analysis frozen into the set's row when the set was recorded, and that analysis is what decides which pause a rep carries. So a document declaring 1.16 still carries BOTH keys on every rep it publishes from a set recorded before this version, with the old quantities in them -- the numbers this change exists to stop publishing. Read a rep carrying both keys as pre-1.16 data whatever the document's `schemaVersion` says, and do not compare its two figures with each other or with a post-1.16 rep's single one. 1.16 carries a SECOND change (#141): a guided set that ends without the guide having called `Done` now speaks and records a terminal cue, `Set ended`. That is a set the lifter ended early AND a guided set given no rep target, which the guide never finishes on its own and which therefore completes normally carrying this word. NOT additive, for the reason 1.4, 1.8, 1.9, 1.12 and the 1.13 `voiceCues` change were not: no key changes type or stops being written, but the contents of an existing array change -- a newly recorded guided set with no `Done` on its track carries one row it did not carry before, and a reader matching only `Done` to find the end of a set now misses that ending. This qualifies 1.12's own list of the cases it leaves unbounded: its third member, a guided set the lifter ended before the prescription was called through, no longer occurs from this version, and the other two -- an ad-hoc set recorded with the voice guide off, and every set recorded before the app wrote cue tracks -- are unchanged. WHAT IT DOES NOT CHANGE, said plainly because the issue that asked for it assumed otherwise: it does not tighten anybody's rep list. The tap that ends a set is the tap that stops the recording, so no sample and therefore no detection can lie past the boundary and none is excluded by it. Measured on the session that found this (17 sets, app 0.1.41): the eleven completed sets keep recording 4.3 to 13.7 s past `Done`, while the five the lifter failed stop 0.482 to 0.832 s after their last spoken cue. startedAt.description: When the session's first recorded set began, as a UTC instant. Always UTC with a `Z` designator, in every schema version. This is the unambiguous moment; `timeZone` is what turns it into a local time of day.

endedAt.description: When the session was closed, as a UTC instant. Same rendering rules as `startedAt`.

timeZone.description: The device's time zone and UTC offset at the moment this session was recorded. Absent means the session predates the app capturing it, which is permanent for those sessions — no artifact records the offset a past session was on, and it is deliberately NOT filled in from the exporting device's current zone, which would be right most of the time and silently wrong after a change of zone. Both members are present or the whole object is absent; there is no half-stated form.

id.description: The zone id the device reported, normally an IANA name such as `America/New_York`. Not guaranteed to be one: a device may report a fixed-offset id like `GMT+05:00`, which yields an offset but names no place. Use it to re-derive the offset at any other instant in the session (this matters only if the session ran across a daylight-saving transition); do not assume it identifies a location.

utcOffsetMinutes.description: Minutes east of UTC in effect at `startedAt`, negative west of it; -240 is US Eastern daylight time. Minutes, not hours, because India (+05:30), Nepal (+05:45) and the Chatham Islands (+12:45) are not whole hours. 0 is a real value — London in winter — and is always written, never omitted as a default. Bounds are the ISO 8601 limits of ±18:00, which are wider than any zone in use.

sessionRpe.description: SESSION RPE on a 1-10 scale: how the whole workout felt to the lifter, stated once by them when they finished it. 1 is a session that barely touched them, 10 is one that took everything. THIS IS A DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT FROM THE PER-SET `rpe` AND THE TWO MUST NEVER BE AVERAGED OR COMPARED AS ONE QUANTITY: a set's `rpe` is how much that ONE set had left in it -- reps-in-reserve at 7-10, load or time headroom below -- and is a statement about one set's proximity to failure; this is the whole session on 1-10, and there are no reps left in a session. The two ranges are identical, so nothing but these descriptions tells a reader which scale a given integer is on. ABSENT MEANS UNRATED, WHICH IS NOT A LOW RATING. The rating is skippable with one tap and a lifter who skips it records no answer; every session recorded before this version is absent for the different reason that the app could not ask; the two are not distinguishable here and both mean the lifter never said. Do not substitute a default, a midpoint or an estimate for an absent value. Where it IS present it is ground truth rather than a proxy: a reader can already estimate session effort by aggregating set RPEs, and this is the lifter's own answer, so prefer it over any such estimate. Not measured, not derived, and not comparable between lifters -- it is one person's report of their own session.

hrvRmssd_ms.description: Session-wide HRV (RMSSD, ms) computed from R-R intervals with artifact rejection.

skippedSets.description: Prescribed sets the lifter deliberately did not do, in the order they were dropped (export 1.21). Omitted when none was. A skipped set has NO entry under exercises: no row was written and nothing was measured. Adherence is recorded-and-not-voided sets over prescribed sets, and an entry here says one of the prescribed sets was dropped on purpose. The absence of entries is NOT evidence that everything prescribed was done: a session that simply ends drops its remainder without writing anything here, and a session recorded before 1.21 could not record a skip at all.

exercise.description: The exercise ID, the same string $defs.exercise.exercise carries, so a skip can be joined to the sets recorded of that movement. Never a display name.

setNumber.description: The set's own number as the PLAN prescribed it, counting from one. The sets that remain of a shortened block keep the numbers the plan gave them, so this is not a position in a list. Where a session runs one movement in two consecutive blocks each block numbers from one, and neither this entry nor the recorded sets say which block it belonged to.

load_kg.description: The load the set is recorded at, body-weight-inclusive on a bodyweight movement. A load corrected on the rest screen after the set is indistinguishable here from one entered before it -- both are the lifter stating what was on the bar -- and the deviation from plannedLoad_kg is what a reader asks. The analysis figures under summary are NOT recomputed on a correction.

load_lb.description: Same load in pounds for convenience; load_kg is canonical.

plannedLoad_kg.description: Present when the set deviated from or followed a plan.

bodyWeight_kg.description: The body weight load_kg was computed with, kilograms, frozen when the set was written (schema 1.19). On body-weight work the recorded load is this plus the added load, which may be NEGATIVE for band or machine assistance, so this is usually the largest term in load_kg and the added or assisting load is load_kg - bodyWeight_kg - exact to within double rounding, not bit-exactly. It is the figure the arithmetic used at the time, not the lifter's weight today: the app stores one body weight and it moves. ABSENT, never 0, and three states share the absence: loaded work, which has no body in the load path and is readable from geometry.bodyweight beside it; a set recorded before this shipped, which no build stored; and a body-weight set recorded while the app held no body weight at all, whose body-weight term was 0 kg. The last two cannot be told apart here. A published 0 would read as a lifter with no mass.

reps.description: How many reps the set is RECORDED as. `repsSource` beside it says WHOSE COUNT this is -- the sensor's live count, the lifter's taps, the cadence guide's schedule, a correction, or the batch segmenter's figure -- and on a timed set nothing counted reps at all, so no word is published and this integer is whatever the segmenter made of one long movement.

plannedPrep_s.description: The prep the PLAN prescribed before this set, in whole seconds. This is the exercise's declared prep_s where the plan declared one, and the app's default where it did not or where the set was recorded without a plan at all -- present either way, because a reader holding prep_s alone cannot tell an adjustment from a declaration. Absent when the set played no prep.

prep_s.description: The prep that played before this set, in whole seconds. Whenever it differs from plannedPrep_s, the lifter adjusted the prep for this exercise in the app; they are equal both when no adjustment exists and when the adjustment happens to equal what the plan prescribed. A plan authored from this export should take prep_s rather than re-guess. 0 is a value, not an absence: it is the prep in which nothing is spoken before the set begins. Absent when the set played no prep. FROM 1.18 THIS KEY IS ABSENT on a set that ended before its work phase began: it carries the prep the app SET OUT to play rather than the prep that elapsed, and on such a set the two provably differ. Read `plannedPrep_s` for the prescription; the raw archive's set descriptor carries the set's own start and end instants, which bound how long the cut-off lead-in actually ran. A set recorded before database v15 carries no answer either way and publishes this key exactly as it always did.

rest_s.description: The rest PRESCRIBED after this set, in whole seconds. Never a measurement of how long the lifter actually rested (#76). From 1.19 the instant it is counted FROM is published rather than left to be inferred: the rest starts when the set was CALLED OVER -- the terminal voice cue on the set's own cue track, which the raw archive carries as that set's `cues` file -- and on a set nothing called over, at the set's own end instant, which is every set recorded with the voice off. A hold whose seconds an armed unit's release decided rests from that release (#259, and from 1.22 on a clock end, #311); from 1.22 (#295) any other timed set the clock ended rests from its `Time` where the timed voice is on; from 1.22 (#288) a timed set the lifter stopped before its clock rests from its `Set ended` where the timed voice is on, unless a release decided its seconds; and any timed set none of these covers rests from its end instant. The countdown the lifter watches and the archive's `rest_before_hrm` stream -- the rest window, written onto the NEXT set -- both begin at that instant, so the two can be joined. The same instant seeds `rest_after_hrm`, the window a session close writes onto the LAST set when there is no next set to carry it forward. Before 1.19 that stream began instead when the set's capture stopped, which on a guided set that spoke `Done` and kept recording was up to 53.06 s later, measured on one field session's thirteen sets; sets that ended at their terminal cue diverged by nothing. The stream may therefore open with samples that also appear in this set's own `hrm` stream: the capture is copied forward, never moved, so every figure computed over `hrm` -- `hr.avgBpm`, `hr.maxBpm`, `hr.endOfSetBpm` -- is unchanged. The stream is NOT continuous from that instant: `endSet` cancels the in-set collector and the app does not enter its rest stage until the set's row is written, so a heart-rate notification landing in that interval reaches neither capture -- 0.08 to 0.58 s on the one session measured. This gap is unmarked in the archive; do not assume uniform coverage across it. A session recorded by an earlier build carries the old window and cannot be corrected, because nothing stored the two instants apart.

scoredPhases.description: Which phases were scored. Pauses are measured and reported but never scored.

actualEccConRatio.description: Measured eccentric:concentric contrast, over the reps that resolved both phases. Reps counted on the drive alone are excluded from both means, so this need not cover every rep of the set.

velocityLoss_pct.description: Best rep to LAST rep, percent -- the drawdown at the point the set was stopped. Absent whenever there is no such figure; `velocityLossBasis` says which case the set is in. A published 0.0 is still possible and means a loss below 0.05 percent, rounded to one decimal; it does not mean the last rep tied the fastest, which is the case that withholds the key instead. WHICH QUESTION IT ANSWERS depends on the set: `velocityLossRegime` beside it says whether this is fatigue or tempo compliance, and reading it as fatigue on a `controlled` set is reading noise as autoregulation. WHICH REPS: from schema 1.22 (#306) the best is taken over the peak-eligible reps only (see summary.peakConVel_mps), and the figure is withheld unless at least two reps are eligible AND the set's last rep is one of them; velocityLossBasis then reads noEligiblePair. A mean drive velocity is a rep's displacement over its drive time, so a rep whose displacement is not bounded gives no bounded velocity to compare either.

velocityLossBasis.description: Which case `velocityLoss_pct` is in. "measured": the figure is present. "notEnoughReps": fewer than two reps were resolved, so there was no pair to take a difference over. "noReference": no peak-eligible rep carried a positive drive velocity to divide by. "terminalRepIsFastest": the last rep resolved was the fastest of the set, which makes best-to-last exactly zero by construction and says nothing about fatigue -- the figure is withheld rather than published as 0.0, and this is also what a detection after the set ended looks like. "noEligiblePair" (schema 1.22, #306): two or more reps were resolved, but fewer than two are peak-eligible -- see summary.peakConVel_mps -- or the last rep is not, so there is no pair the analysis can bound; on every committed field capture with two or more reps this is the word, because almost no rep's displacement is bounded. Present whenever the set resolved any reps, including when `velocityLoss_pct` is absent; absent only when no reps were resolved at all, the same condition under which `repMetricsComplete` is absent.

velocityLossRegime.description: Which QUESTION this set's `velocityLoss_pct` is an answer to. `maxIntent`: the lifter drove every concentric as hard as they could, so a slowing rep is a tiring lifter and the figure is fatigue -- read it as autoregulation, as this document has always told you to. `controlled`: a prescribed tempo fixed the drive's speed, so the figure measures how well the lifter held the count rather than how much capacity they spent; read `tempoCompliance`, `summary.romSpread_pct` and the set's `rpe` as the autoregulation figures there, and read `velocityLoss_pct` as compliance. THE RULE: `maxIntent` when the set has no `tempoPrescribed`, or its `geometry.kind` is `explosive`, or the prescribed tempo's CONCENTRIC digit is `X`; `controlled` otherwise. The concentric digit is read from `geometry` PLANE FIRST. On `geometry.plane` `horizontal` digit 3 is the concentric by phase, whatever `geometry.concentric` says, because a seated row or a chest press has no up or down for a positional reading to attach to. Only on `vertical` is it positional -- digit 3 while `geometry.concentric` is `up`, digit 1 when it is `down`, on a leg curl, a lat pulldown or a pushdown. So `30X0` is `maxIntent` on a bench press and on any horizontal machine, and `controlled` on a leg curl, where the X is the return. A velocity target plays no part. `velocityLoss_pct` IS STILL PUBLISHED IN BOTH; this key says how to read it, it does not withhold it. AND THIS KEY IS PUBLISHED ON EVERY SET THE RULE CAN PLACE A WORD ON, including sets carrying no `velocityLoss_pct` at all -- one too short for a best-to-last figure, one whose last resolved rep was its fastest, one with no eligible pair (1.22) -- because it names which question the figure WOULD answer, and that question is settled by the prescription and the geometry rather than by whether the figure came out. That is the opposite of `rpeScale`, which is omitted on a set with no `rpe`. DERIVED at export time from `tempoPrescribed` and `geometry`, both already on the row, so a set re-exported by a build carrying this key gains the word however long ago it was recorded. ABSENT where the regime is not decidable, and absence is a state rather than a hedge: a set with no `geometry` (every set recorded before that column existed), a hold or a carry, which has no concentric for the question to be about, and a tempo string the app cannot parse. Read an absent key exactly as you read every set before this key existed, which is `maxIntent`'s reading. A VERTICAL concentric-DOWN lift carrying a tempo is always `controlled`, because the plan contract accepts `X` only in digit 3 and its digit 1 is therefore always a number. HORIZONTAL work is not in that position -- its concentric IS digit 3 -- so `30X0` on a chest press or a chest-supported row is `maxIntent` under today's contract however `geometry.concentric` was declared.

refusedDetections.description: How many detections the analyzer judged were NOT reps of this set, removing them from the list every other figure here is computed over - schema 1.19, issue #125. The rule: a detection that resolved no eccentric partner AND whose rom_m exceeds 4.5x the median rom_m of the set's other detections is not a rep. The bound is relative to the set's own reps rather than absolute, because the equipment's travel does not change within a set and an absolute range bound would need a figure per exercise. ABSENT, 0 and a positive number are three different facts. Absent: fewer than four detections resolved, so no median of others existed to derive a bound from - or the set was recorded before this version, which is permanent, because the value is frozen into the stored analysis when the set is analysed and nothing re-runs the segmenter at export time. 0: a bound was derived and refused nothing. Positive: that many detections were removed. THIS IS NOT A COUNT OF THE SET'S PHANTOMS. The bound is fitted to the app's committed capture corpus and is placed to err toward admitting a bad detection rather than refusing a real rep - a refused real rep would move velocityLoss_pct, which is best rep to LAST rep, against the wrong rep. The eccentric-partner clause is not decoration: the corpus holds a two-phase detection ABOVE the bound, and that clause is the only thing keeping it. A 0 means nothing was far enough out to refuse, never that the set's figures are sound. NOTHING IS DELETED: the set's raw IMU stream is published unchanged and any refused detection can be re-derived from it.

refusedDetectionReason.description: Why refusedDetections is non-zero, and absent whenever that key is absent or 0. "unpairedRangeOutlier": a detection with no eccentric partner whose range is an outlier against the set's own reps. Named for both clauses on purpose - a paired detection at the same range is kept, so this is not a range cap.

detectionsBeforeWorkStart.description: How many detections finished before this set's WORK began and are therefore not reps of it, removing them from the list every other figure here is computed over - schema 1.19, issue #245. The rule: a detection whose DRIVE ENDED before the instant the set's prep ended is not a rep. The drive's end and not its start, so a drive begun during the prep and still under way when the work started is KEPT - the mirror of the straddling drive the terminal-cue bound keeps at the other end, and the direction that errs toward admitting a countdown movement rather than refusing a real first rep. ABSENT, 0 and a positive number are three different facts. Absent: the set has no work-start instant - an ad-hoc set that ran no prep, a set ended while its prep was still running, or any set recorded before that instant was stored, which is permanent. 0: an instant bounded this set's head and nothing came before it. Positive: that many detections were removed. A SEPARATE KEY FROM refusedDetections RATHER THAN A SECOND VALUE OF refusedDetectionReason, because the two ABSENCES mean different things: refusedDetections is absent when a set resolved fewer than four detections, this is absent when a set has no instant, and a heavy triple with a known instant is in one state and not the other. NOTHING IS DELETED: the set's raw IMU stream and its prep window are both published unchanged, so any excluded detection can be re-derived from them.

artefactSamples.description: How many samples in this set's analysed IMU stream carry a total support acceleration above 4 g - readings a lifted implement cannot produce - schema 1.21, issues #290 and #255. THE BOUND'S PROVENANCE: the magnitude includes gravity, so an implement at rest reads 1 g; net drive on a tempo-prescribed set stays well under 1 g, putting the exercise's own ceiling near 2 g; 4 g admits three g of net drive, which nothing a lifter does to a loaded bar reaches. The sensor's full scale is 16 g, measured from a deadlift capture whose samples read 15.999 g at the instant the bar met the floor - a sample AT the range does not even bound the real acceleration from below. WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY: not that the sample is corrupt. A deadlift's floor contact is a REAL mechanical event above this bound; what it is not is lift kinematics, and a peak taken across it describes the plate hitting the floor. WHAT IT CHANGES: a rep whose own span carries one is excluded from summary.peakConVel_mps and summary.peakPower_w (and, from 1.22, from the velocityLoss_pct pair), which is why this key is published in the summary-only export too. NOTHING IS REPAIRED and no sample is altered: substituting an out-of-range reading before the velocity integration moves the rep COUNT on nine of eleven committed captures that carry one and cannot recover a railed sample at all, so the figure is withheld and counted instead. ABSENT, 0 and a positive number are three different facts. Absent: the set was analysed before this count existed, which is permanent - it is frozen into the stored analysis and nothing re-runs the estimator at export time. 0: the stream was counted and carried none. Positive: that many samples could not have been measured. NOT THE SUM OF THE PER-REP COUNTS: this is over the whole stream and includes samples between detections and samples the set-end and work-start bounds excluded.

hr.description: Heart rate for this set, summarised over the samples the strap's own report supports. Absent when the strap reported nothing usable, and equally absent when no strap was connected -- the two cannot be told apart from this document, and the raw per-set HRM CSV in the accompanying archive is the only place the difference is visible.

endOfSetBpm.description: Heart rate at the LAST sample of the set, present only when that sample is itself usable. Never backfilled from an earlier sample: this key names a time as much as a value.

minBpm.description: The lowest heart rate this set's trusted samples support -- the same population avgBpm and maxBpm are drawn from, never the whole stream. Present only when at least one sample is trusted; never zero, which would read as a measurement rather than nothing to measure.

repMetrics.description: Per-rep detail; present only in detailed exports.

voiceCues.description: Spoken voice cues during the set ('Down', 'Hold', 'Up', 'Drive', 'Return', '3', 'Ready', 'Brace', 'Rep 4', 'Last rep', 'Done', 'Set ended', 'Time'...), stamped in epoch ms on the same clock as the raw IMU/HR streams so they can be cross-referenced with accelerometer data. Detailed export only. A bare digit is a TEMPO COUNT -- the guide counting a stroke out second by second, or a timed set counting down -- and never a rep number; a rep is always named in full, as 'Rep 4' or as 'Last rep'. From 1.20 the counts of a stroke whose word a rep number replaced continue FROM that number, so a three-second stroke publishes '2' then '3' and its '1' is the rep call: a digit is still a tempo count, and the lowest digit of a stroke is no longer necessarily '1'. From 1.19 a guided call names the rep the guide is calling for -- 'Rep 4' as the fourth rep falls due, and 'Last rep' for the final one, which is why no guided set says 'Rep N' for its planned N; before 1.19 the same call counted FINISHED reps, so a 'Rep 4' row named the rep behind the one being lifted and 'Last rep' fell on the rep before the last. From 1.20, on a schedule with a free second at the START of the rep, a guided call opens the rep it names: it is spoken on that rep's first second, in place of that rep's first stroke word (#293). A schedule with NO free second there -- two one-second strokes and no closing pause -- names the rep at the end of the drive instead, on the lifts whose drive OPENS the rep: the number is spoken on the beat that opens as the concentric ends, in place of that beat's word, on every rep including rep 1 (#266). So a 1010 press publishes 'Up', 'Rep 1', 'Up', 'Rep 2' and so on, and a set of six publishes 'Rep 1' through 'Rep 5' then 'Last rep'; the word the number replaces -- the return's, or a mid-rep 'Hold' -- appears nowhere in such a set, so a consumer counting stroke rows to count reps gets zero on one and must count the call rows, one per rep. A set of ONE on such a schedule publishes 'Last rep' and no number, the rep in hand being the planned last from its first rep. The same prescription on a lift whose drive CLOSES the rep publishes no call at all, exactly as before 1.20. On a set recorded from 1.13 through 1.19 WHEN a call is heard depends on the schedule and is not uniform: on the two schedules that merged the call into a stroke it is spoken during the rep it names, and on the schedule whose prescription ends in a pause it is spoken in the previous rep's closing pause, before the rep it names has begun. That holds for 'Last rep' exactly as it does for a number, either side of 1.20, and which schedule a set used is not readable from the tempo string alone. The UNGUIDED counter runs on a different clock and is unchanged either side of 1.19: it speaks as a rep completes, so its 'Rep N' counts finished reps and its 'Last rep' lands as rep N-1 completes. Nothing in a row says which counter spoke it, and from 1.19 the two disagree by one, so the distinction matters where before it did not. The only discriminator is the metronome's own stroke words: a guided track carries at least one of them in every rep -- 'Down' and 'Up' on vertical work, 'Drive' and 'Return' on horizontal, and from 1.22 'Drive' on vertical work as well, in place of 'Up' on a drive the tempo writes as 'X' -- so 'Drive' is NOT evidence of horizontal work, and geometry.plane is what says which plane a set was -- and both in rep 1, so a track carrying rep calls and no stroke word came from the unguided counter, whose whole vocabulary is bare digits, 'Rep N', 'Last rep' and 'Done'. A track recorded before 1.20 carries both words in every rep; from 1.20 the rep number takes the first stroke word's second on every rep after the first, so THAT word is published once per set -- rep 1's -- while the other stroke's word is published on every rep. A reader counting stroke rows to count reps must count the call rows instead, one per rep after the first, each on its rep's first second, plus rep 1's own stroke word -- except on a set that counts at the end of the drive, where the replaced word is published on NO rep and the call rows are one per rep with none to add. 'Hold' is NOT one of those words and must not be read as one: it is a pause the prescription asked for, absent from every tempo without a mid-rep pause, and it is also the word a timed HOLD set's prep speaks. On a set recorded from 1.13 through 1.19 two rows may carry the same instant, and that is NOT a duplicate: the guide merged a rep call into a stroke's own word and spoke them as one utterance ('Down, Rep 3'), because the speech engine cancels whatever it was saying when a new utterance arrives, and both words were said so both were written, at one clock reading taken once -- the stroke word first, the call second. From 1.20 the call REPLACES that word rather than riding beside it, so no two rows share an instant on a guided track and the replaced word is not written at all. A sentence here used to tell a consumer matching stroke rows that it was unaffected; it is deleted rather than qualified, because from 1.20 such a consumer matches one row per SET on the geometry whose first stroke is the one it matches. What this array is NOT: a record of the reps performed. It is what the app SAID, on the metronome's own schedule, whether or not the lifter followed it -- repMarks is what was counted. Sets recorded before the app wrote the merged call carry the stroke word alone, and nothing in the row distinguishes a set that spoke no call from one that spoke it and did not write it down. A track may also end on `Set ended`, which is NOT the same ending as `Done`: `Done` means the prescription was called all the way through, `Set ended` means the guide never called `Done`: the lifter stopped a guided set early -- the failure tile, or the early exit offered during the lead-in -- or the set had no rep target for the guide to finish, in which case it is an ordinary completion. It is NOT on its own evidence that a set was failed; read `failed` for that. From 1.22 (#288) `Set ended` also ends a timed set the lifter stopped before its clock did, where the timed voice is on -- a hold or a carry ended before `Time`, or a timed set with no target, which has no `Time` to reach -- so on a timed set's track it is not evidence the set was guided. Both are spoken aloud and both bound the set's rep list at their own instant; a reader wanting the moment a set was called over should look for either, or for `Time` on a timed set (from 1.22, #295). From 1.22 (#295) `Time` is itself terminal: it is what a timed set's own clock says on the tick that ends the set, so it bounds that set's working window -- the raw archive's `rollExcursion_deg` runs from work start to it, and where the work start is on the record its `rollExcursionBasis` reads `workingWindow` -- and the rest after such a set is counted from it unless a release decided the seconds. It is NOT evidence the lifter held to the end: a hold let go before its target and never tapped still hears it, and `durationEndedBy` says what the seconds were measured to. From 1.16 every guided set carries exactly one of the two. A guided set whose track carries neither was recorded before 1.16. On those, a track ending on a stroke means the guide never called `Done` and the app wrote no terminal word -- the lifter ended the set early, or the set had no rep target for the guide to finish. The record cannot tell those two apart; read `failed` and `reps` against the prescription.

t_ms.description: Epoch milliseconds when the cue was spoken.

repMarks.description: The instants a rep was COUNTED during this set, epoch milliseconds on the same clock as the raw IMU, heart-rate and cue streams. Detailed export only, the same terms voiceCues is published on. What was counted, never what the bar did: a mark is written when the lifter taps the rep button or when the voice guide calls a rep, so on a straight-rep set carrying no tempo these are the only per-rep instants anywhere in this document -- repMetrics entries carry durations and an ordinal position and no clock, and voiceCues is what the app SAID rather than what was counted. Absent rather than empty, and the absence is weak: a sensor-counted set produces no marks at all, and neither does any set recorded before the app stored them, and nothing here tells those two apart; neither is evidence that no rep was performed. The number of marks may disagree with reps, in both directions -- a rest-screen correction rewrites reps and cannot reach a mark already written, and the guide calls a rep on its own schedule whether or not the lifter followed it. Where they disagree, reps is what the set was recorded as and this is what was counted while it happened.

items.description: Epoch milliseconds at which a rep was counted.

peakConVel_mps.description: Best instantaneous concentric (drive) velocity across the set, metres per second. From schema 1.22 (#306) over the PEAK-ELIGIBLE reps only: a rep whose own span carries a sample above the physical bound (artefactSamples, 1.21), whose guard band -- the 0.4 s before its span -- carries one (guardArtefactSamples), or whose displacement is not bounded (romBounded false) is left out, and a rep carrying none of those keys (an older recording) is kept. ABSENT when no rep is eligible, and ABSENT when the best eligible peak falls below summary.meanConVel_mps, which is taken over every rep: a peak below the set's own mean is not a peak. A consumer taking the max over repMetrics[].peakConVel_mps will not reproduce this figure. Absent is not zero.

meanRom_m.description: Mean rom_m over the reps whose displacement the analysis can bound, from schema 1.21 (#291) -- see romBounded on each repMetrics row. A consumer averaging repMetrics[].rom_m will not reproduce it. ABSENT, never 0, when NO rep of the set is bounded: one bounded rep is enough for a mean where the spread beside it needs two. Absent on every one of the committed field captures this rule was measured on, which is not every field capture the repository holds, because a rep is bounded only where the drift correction's erasure was capped over every inter-anchor interval its span crosses, and on a real working set the bar never goes quiet enough for that.

romSpread_pct.description: How far the reps of this set disagree with each other about rom_m: the population standard deviation as a percentage of meanRom_m. A machine has one travel and a lifter range of motion varies a little, so a large value says the displacements the set derived channels rest on do not agree with each other. Over the reps whose displacement the analysis can bound, from schema 1.21 -- see romBounded on each repMetrics row (#291). ABSENT, never 0, when fewer than two of this set's reps are bounded, or when those reps average no displacement at all - dispersion is undefined there and a number would be a claim about evidence that does not exist. ALSO ABSENT ON ALMOST EVERY REAL SET for the first of those reasons: of the committed field captures this rule was measured on, which is not every field capture the repository holds, NO rep is bounded, so read an absent value as - the analysis cannot bound these displacements - and never as a small spread. Published at n=2, where it is real but weak; read it against the rep count. WHAT IT CANNOT TELL YOU: it does not separate a segmenter that mismeasured a good set from a lifter whose range genuinely varied, and if a capture ever shows high spread with segmentation known to be correct then this figure is decoration rather than diagnosis. The seated leg curl rail, whose travel is fixed at 0.4-0.5 m, cannot be used to test that any more: none of its own reps are bounded either, so the check has to be made against repMetrics[].rom_m directly rather than against this figure.

peakPower_w.description: Best instantaneous concentric (drive) power across the set, watts. From schema 1.22 (#306) over the same peak-eligible reps summary.peakConVel_mps is -- no artefactSamples in the span, no guardArtefactSamples in the band, romBounded not false -- and ABSENT when none is eligible or when the best eligible peak falls below summary.meanConPower_w. A consumer taking the max over repMetrics[].peakPower_w will not reproduce this figure. Absent is not zero.

meanConPower_w.description: Mean of per-rep average concentric power, watts.

noRepsReason.description: Why this set resolved no reps - schema 1.18. The one key in this object written when every other key is absent, and the only thing separating a set whose velocity reconstruction ran away from a manual set recorded with no sensor at all: both otherwise publish reps: [], summary: {} and no velocityLossBasis. Each value names why the rep list is empty and claims nothing about the bar or the lifter. afterSetEndCue: reps were resolved and the set's own end cue excluded all of them, so segmentation did not fail. noMovement: no sample left the pause band. runsExceedDisplacementCap: more than half the set's movement runs displaced further than any real phase can, which the DSP reads as unanchored integration drift. runsBelowStartThreshold: no movement run survived demotion, and at least as many failed on peak speed as on duration - a tie is included here and reads as too slow. runsTooBrief: no movement run survived demotion, and more of them failed on duration than on peak speed. phasesUnpaired: runs survived and none paired into a rep. driveBelowMinRom: every drive the pairing walk reached fell under the minimum range of motion - on a concentric-first lift the drive alone is the rep, so no pair need have been formed. ABSENT ON A SET THAT RESOLVED ANY REP AT ALL, including one that resolved 1 of 10 performed - its absence is not a statement that the reps are right. Absent too on every set recorded before 1.18: the value is frozen into the stored analysis when the set is recorded and nothing re-runs the segmenter at export time. beforeWorkStart: reps were resolved, the set's own end cue kept some of them, and every one it kept finished before the set's WORK began - schema 1.19, issue #245, and like afterSetEndCue it is not a segmentation failure. mountNotDeclared: the segmenter was NEVER RUN - schema 1.20, issue #247 - because the analysis had moved off the unit the set armed (sensors.analysedFellBack is true) and the geometry block declares a MOUNT rather than only the lift: sensorOnStack true, sensorInverted true, or travelRatio other than 1.0. That declaration belongs to the ARMED unit, and running the DSP over a different unit under it swaps the concentric and the eccentric outright at a rep count that need not move with it - identical on the synthetic negation pair, 13 under the declared stack geometry against 18 under the lifter-side one on field-38 set 14's partner - so no figures are published rather than inverted ones. The raw stream of every unit is archived as usual and the set can be re-derived from it under any geometry. It is the only value set before the segmenter runs at all.

duration_s.description: Hold/carry seconds recorded for timed sets. Since 1.13 a timed set ends when its clock reaches the seconds the set was WORKING TO -- plannedDuration_s unless the lifter changed the hold in the change-set dialog, in which case theirs -- so this equals plannedDuration_s only on a set that ran to its target AND was not changed by the lifter; a set the lifter ended by hand carries what it actually lasted, or -- from 1.21, where an armed unit's stream showed the implement being let go and believing it takes 1 to 20 s off -- the span to that release rather than to the tap, which is SHORTER than the same set would have published under 1.20 by the length of the walk back to the phone, and a set the lifter corrected afterwards on the rest screen carries the corrected figure. From 1.22 (#311) a HOLD the CLOCK ended carries the same span to a release instead of the target where its armed unit saw the implement let go and believing it takes 1 to 20 whole seconds off the target, so such a set is SHORTER than its target though the clock ran to it; a release at or after the target, or none, leaves the target. From 1.22 (#314) a CARRY the clock ended carries the target whatever its stream shows: no walking-carry stream has been captured, and a footstrike could read as a release. Which of them produced the figure is durationEndedBy from 1.21; the sentence that stood here -- that corrected and measured seconds are not distinguishable and that reps publish repsManual while duration has no counterpart -- is deleted rather than reworded. FROM 1.18 THIS KEY IS ABSENT on a set that ended before its work phase began; such a set carries `abandonedInPrep` instead. Before 1.18 it published 0 there, and that 0 was never a measurement. A set recorded before database v15 carries no answer either way and publishes this key exactly as it always did.

durationEndedBy.description: 1.21: which of four things decided the duration_s beside this key (#259, #249). clock -- the app's own clock reached the target and ended the set, so duration_s IS the target and the lifter heard Time a beat before it; from 1.22 (#311), on a HOLD, only where its armed unit, if any, reported no release taking 1 to 20 whole seconds off the target; a timed CARRY the clock ended is never offered the release (#314), so it reads clock and its target whatever its stream shows. sensor -- an armed unit's stream showed the implement being let go, and duration_s runs to THAT instant rather than to the tap that followed it -- or, from 1.22 (#311), rather than to the target on a hold the clock ended, where the release came 1 to 20 whole seconds before the target, so a sensor hold may never have been tapped at all; on a hands-full hold the tap is 5-10 s late by the owner's own account and every one of those seconds used to be inside the figure. lifter -- the tap decided and nothing else spoke, because no unit was armed or the armed unit's stream carried no release, so the reach is still inside duration_s. corrected -- the lifter restated the figure on the rest screen afterwards, REPLACING whichever of the other three stood before it, so a corrected figure does not also say what produced the figure it replaced; the raw span stays recoverable from the archive's workStartedAt_ms and the row's end instant. ABSENT, never defaulted, on a set that is not timed and on every timed set recorded before database v19, where absence means the build could not say rather than that the lifter ended it.

abandonedInPrep.description: True when the set ENDED BEFORE ITS WORK PHASE BEGAN -- the lifter's tap started the recording, the lead-in was still running, and the set was over before the clock or the cadence started (1.18, #216). It is a statement about the CAPTURE and not about the lifter: the same write path is taken by a set abandoned during its lead-in for any reason, including a slot the app should not have armed at all. What follows from it: `duration_s` and `prep_s` are absent because neither was measured, `reps` is 0 because nothing was counted rather than because nothing was lifted, and any `failed` on such a set is the app's derivation -- read `failedByLifter` to confirm. The raw stream is still real and still worth reading; what it captured is a lead-in. OMITTED WHEN FALSE, and omission is NOT proof of the opposite: whether the work began is a database column added at v15, so every set recorded before it carries no answer and publishes nothing here. A missing key means "the work began, or the app could not tell".

side.description: Unilateral sets: the arm the set WORKED. Since 1.17 (#215) this is the lifter's own statement where they made one on the change-next-set control, and the plan's prescription otherwise; read it against `plannedSide` beside it, and where the two differ the lifter swapped arm order. BEFORE 1.17 this key was a copy of the plan's own declaration -- the app had nowhere to record a worked side -- so on an older document it says what was PRESCRIBED and is silent about what was worked, and a reader who took it for either was right only by accident.

plannedSide.description: Unilateral sets: the arm the PLAN prescribed, frozen when the set was recorded (1.17, #215). ABSENT, never null and never a copy of `side`, on bilateral work, on an ad-hoc set and on a set the lifter appended -- none of those was prescribed a side -- and on every set recorded before database v14, where the column did not exist. So absence does NOT mean the lifter worked what was asked: it means nothing asked, or the set predates the pair. Nothing backfills it, because on those older rows `side` WAS the prescription and copying it across would assert that the app knew which limb moved.

rpe.description: PER-SET RPE on a 1-10 scale: how much THIS ONE SET had left in it. Logged when the set ends; correctable afterward on the rest screen. ONE QUESTION, ANCHORED IN TWO UNITS, because the resolution a lifter can supply changes with the distance from failure. Since 1.14 the app's grid offers exactly seven rungs: 10 nothing left, 9 one rep left, 8 two reps left, 7 three reps left -- reps-in-reserve, in that movement's own words on a hold or an explosive lift -- then three HEADROOM rungs, whose noun is the EXERCISE's own from 1.19 and is named by `rpeScale`. On a `load` scale the captions are authored per unit and never converted: 6 'could have added 10-15 lb' or 'could have added 5 kg', 4 '20-30 lb' or '10 kg', 1 'much more'. On `time`: 6 'could have gone about 15 s longer', 4 'about 30 s longer', 1 'much longer'. On `reps`: 6 'About 3-4 reps left', 4 'Five or more reps left', 1 'Many more reps left' -- above the counted end, which already covers three and below. On `feel`, for an exercise declared "none": 6 'Comfortable — some left', 4 'Easy — plenty left', 1 'Very easy', naming no quantity at all. The pound band spans two equipment increments, 10 lb on a bar and 15 lb on a stack, because the app has no declared increment anywhere and cannot know which is in front of the lifter -- so the tile names a WEIGHT and never a notch. WHICH SCALE THE LIFTER WAS ASKED ON IS RECORDED, in `rpeScale`, and a 6 cannot be read without it: the same integer is a plate claim on one exercise and a rep claim on another. That key is absent on every set recorded before 1.19, where the rule is `load` on a dynamic set and `time` on a timed one. THIS EXPORT DOES NOT RECORD which unit's caption was on screen for a given set; read the session's own unit if that matters. A TIMED 4 CHANGED MEANING AT 1.19, from 'about a minute longer' to 'about 30 s longer', and a timed 6 from '15-30 s longer' to 'about 15 s'; nothing rewrites stored values. The figures in seconds are authored rather than measured; the pound and kilogram bands come from the equipment the lifter actually meets. 2, 3 and 5 are valid values carrying no tile: the gaps exist so the anchors sort, and a value there is a real point on the same ruler rather than corrupt data. WHAT A PRE-1.14 VALUE MEANT: the grid then offered 6 to 10 only and 6 was its floor, 'easy, 4+ reps left', absorbing everything 1 and 4 now take; 7 through 10 are unchanged. Nothing rewrites stored values. THIS IS A DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT FROM THE SESSION-LEVEL `sessionRpe`, which is the lifter's 1-10 answer for the whole workout; the two ranges are now identical and the two must never be averaged or compared as one quantity. From 1.22 (#313) a set that FAILED carries no rpe, whichever of the two failure facts says so -- the lifter's tap, or a shortfall the app derived from the recorded reps or seconds. The owner's rule is that a failed set is not rated, so a rating already standing when a failure arrives -- a hold rated and then corrected below 90 % of its target, or a count corrected short of the plan -- is cleared by the same write, and a rating given beside a failure is not stored; `failedByLifter` is unchanged by it. A set recorded by an earlier build may carry both.

rpeScale.description: WHICH QUESTION this set's `rpe` answers (1.19, #244). `load` means the headroom rungs named a weight the lifter could have added; `reps` a count of reps left; `time` seconds a hold could have run on; `feel` a bare feeling with no quantity, which is what an exercise declared "none" is asked for. It names the HEADROOM rungs 1, 4 and 6 only -- the counted end, 7 through 10, is reps in reserve on every scale. The word is chosen by the EXERCISE's declared `progression` and is FROZEN when the set is recorded, never derived at export: a plan is editable and deletable, and the resolved word rather than the declaration is stored so that a later change to how a declaration maps onto a question cannot restate which question a past lifter saw. ABSENT on every set recorded before 1.19, where the reading rule is what the app asked then -- `load` on a dynamic set, `time` on a timed one -- which says nothing about what that exercise progressed on, because nothing recorded it and nothing backfills it. ALSO ABSENT on a set carrying no `rpe`, since the word qualifies the number and is published beside it or not at all. Absence is never a fifth value.

failed.description: True when the set is marked failed: the lifter tapped it as failed, the set fell short of its planned reps or duration and the app derived a failure, or both. The derived case needs no lifter input at all. WHICH OF THE TWO a given set carries is `failedByLifter`, from 1.18; without it a tapped failure and a derived one are indistinguishable here.

failedByLifter.description: Whether the LIFTER called this set failed, rather than the app deriving it from a shortfall (1.18, #216, #169).
